title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: MSF budget increase
sections.summary: MSF's budget will rise about 18%, from $3.9 billion in FY2020 to an estimated $4.6 billion in FY2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In my Budget debate speech, I spoke about how this term of Government will see the Ministry of Social and Family Development's (MSF's) budget increase by about 18%, from $3.9 billion in FY2020, to an estimated $4.6 billion in FY2024.

sections.label: Enhanced family support schemes
sections.summary: Baby Bonus, CDA grants, ComLink and KidSTART have been enhanced or expanded to support families and children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We have enhanced the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant and the Government CDA co-matching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We have expanded ComLink nationwide to cover 14,000 families with children living in rental housing to sustain social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: And we have expanded KidSTART, which provides support in the development of children from low-income families up to age six.

sections.label: ComLink+ support for families
sections.summary: The passage asks MSF to share how ComLink+ will better support lower-income families in improving their life outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can MSF share more information about how will the new ComLink+ better support lower-income families in their efforts towards improving their life outcomes and building a better future for themselves?

sections.label: Volunteerism rates decline
sections.summary: Volunteerism rates peaked at 35% in 2016 and fell to about 22% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Volunteerism rates peaked in 2016 at 35%, before coming down to about 22% in 2023.

sections.label: Families for Life and counselling
sections.summary: The passage asks about expanding Families for Life, take-up of free FSC marital counselling, and improving access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: How does MSF intend to expand the Families for Life Movement and galvanise whole-of-society effort towards strengthening families in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: What is the take-up rate for the free marital counselling offered by our Family Service Centres (FSCs)?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Can we improve access to such counselling, by offering them, for example, at every community centre?

sections.label: Enhancing Family Service Centres
sections.summary: The passage asks what MSF plans to enhance FSCs so they can better support vulnerable families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: What are MSF's plans to enhance the FSCs, so that they can better support the vulnerable families in our community?

sections.label: Family for Life expansion
sections.summary: The Family for Life movement led by MSF is yielding promising results and will expand to 24 towns by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I know that the Family for Life movement led by MSF is yielding promising results in activating a supportive community environment for family bonding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am also glad to know that the Family for Life at Community will be expanded to 24 towns nationwide by 2025.

sections.label: Anchor operator monthly fees
sections.summary: Monthly fees for anchor operators would have fallen from $800 in 2019 to $640 in 2025 before GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: In this term of Government, monthly fees for anchor operators would have come down significantly from $800 in 2019 to $640 in 2025, before Goods and Services Tax (GST).

sections.label: Preschool participation in rental flats
sections.summary: MSF states 2021 preschool participation of Singaporean children aged three to four in public rental flats was about 80%, below the 88% national average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: According to MSF, the 2021 preschool participation rate of Singaporean children aged three to four years residing in public rental flats was about 80%, lower than the national average of about 88%.

sections.label: Fertility rate historic low
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate fell to a historic low of 0.97 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Chairman, I was dismayed to hear that Singapore's total fertility rate (TFR) fell to a historic low of 0.97 in 2023.

sections.label: Infant care subsidies
sections.summary: Infant care services at institutional Anchor and Partner Operators are currently subsidised by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Infant care services at institutional Anchor and Partner Operators are currently subsidised by the Government.

sections.label: Household Services Scheme childminding
sections.summary: MOM's Household Services Scheme allows companies to recruit migrant workers for basic childminding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) currently has a Household Services Scheme (HSS) that allows companies to recruit migrant workers for basic childminding.

sections.label: Early childhood education costs
sections.summary: The passage states that early childhood education costs are higher on average than primary and secondary school, despite high returns.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The need to promote such investments almost certainly informed the decision to create the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But despite its clear importance and the fact that returns are the highest in these early stages, the costs of sending a child for early childhood education are still higher on average than sending them to higher levels, like primary and secondary school.

sections.label: Preschool enrolment of three to four year olds
sections.summary: In 2021, 88% of children aged three to four were not enrolled in preschool, dropping to 78% among lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2021, 88% of children aged three to four were not enrolled in preschool.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And perhaps more worryingly, this drops to 78% among lower-income families.

sections.label: Subsidy distinction for working mothers
sections.summary: One strategy is to eliminate the distinction between subsidies for families with a working mother and those without, for lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One strategy is to simply eliminate the distinction between subsidies made available to families with a working mother versus those without, for lower-income households.

sections.label: Childminding services as infant care option
sections.summary: The Government intends to introduce affordable, safe and reliable childminding services as an additional infant care option for families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: As part of the Forward SG report, I understand the Government intends to introduce affordable, safe and reliable childminding services as an additional infant care option for families.

sections.label: MSF preschool affordability and support
sections.summary: The passage asks what MSF is doing to improve preschool affordability and quality, and financial support for families with special needs children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With the rising demand for preschool places over the years and the cost-of-living issues, what is MSF doing to further improve the affordability and quality of preschools for all families in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How will MSF, too, look into more financial support at preschools for families with special needs children?

sections.label: Early childhood educator attrition rate
sections.summary: The annual attrition rate of early childhood educators was five times higher than the general Ministry of Education attrition rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The annual attrition rate of early childhood educators was five times higher than the general Ministry of Education (MOE) attrition rate.

sections.label: SPARK Developmental Visits frequency
sections.summary: The speaker suggests more frequent, random SPARK Developmental Visits and more assessor visits to observe classroom interactions instead of paper audits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We must ensure that the sector is as much teacher-centric as it is child-centric for quality education to be sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I suggest that we make SPARK Developmental Visits more frequent and random, than only once in three years; and assessors should visit centres more often to observe the classroom interactions rather than rely on a paper audit exercise.

sections.label: Family coaches-to-ComLink families ratio
sections.summary: The speaker asks what the family coaches-to-ComLink families ratio will be as the enhancements are rolled out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: One, what will be the family coaches-to-ComLink families ratio as the enhancements are rolled out?

sections.label: Beneficiaries-to-coach and befrienders ratio
sections.summary: The speaker recommends MSF maintain a low beneficiaries-to-coach and befrienders ratio and welcomes debt repayment assistance to licensed moneylenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2022, I have highlighted the importance of a good interpersonal relationship between the beneficiaries and the case worker in order to optimise the effectiveness of the assistance and support rendered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I recommend that MSF maintain a low beneficiaries-to-coach and befrienders ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will not only ensure that beneficiaries' families get adequate support from their coach and befrienders, it can also help reduce burnout and stress on the coaches and befrienders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I also welcome the introduction of assistance with debt repayment to licensed moneylending companies and organisations that are trackable and verifiable.

sections.label: Financial literacy in secondary curriculum
sections.summary: The speaker recommends that MSF and MOE explore integrating basic financial literacy into the secondary school curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Additionally, Sir, I would recommend that MSF and MOE explore integrating basic financial literacy into the curriculum for secondary school students.

sections.label: ComLink+ family coaches and incentives
sections.summary: ComLink+, piloted and now to be scaled, provides family coaches and financial incentives for families uplifting themselves in preschool education, employment, financial stability and home ownership saving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: ComLink+, piloted and now to be scaled, provides for family coaches and also financial incentives for families who actively uplift themselves in these four areas: preschool education, employment, financial stability and saving for home ownership.

sections.label: ComLink+ pilot update and coordination
sections.summary: The speaker seeks an update on the ComLink+ pilot's progress, lessons, strategies for multiple contact points, and measures ensuring suitable, reliable, committed volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In addition, despite MSF's efforts, there are still many well-meaning donors and volunteers who are unaware of or prefer to do their own thing, leading to numerous uncoordinated touch points; conflicting advice or support; service overlaps and hindering a family's ability to follow a coherent uplift plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I seek an update from MSF now regarding: one, the progress, including the number of families served and the impact of the ComLink+ pilot to date; two, lessons learned from the pilot, including challenges and the resources required; three, strategies to address the issue of multiple points of contact so the family coach can be more effective; and four, measures to ensure that volunteers recruited to assist ComLink families are suitable, reliable and committed and do not just walk in and out of the lives of these families.

sections.label: ComLink+ support for rental families
sections.summary: ComLink+ nudges rental families to send kids to preschool, stay employed and save, described as empowerment beyond ComCare's safety net.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Essentially, nudging families in rental housing to send their kids to preschool, stay in good jobs and build savings, positive behaviours that help equalise opportunities for their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: If ComCare is assistance to meet today's needs, ComLink+ is empowerment to build tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: If ComCare is a safety net by the state, ComLink+ is a trampoline formed by all of us.

sections.label: Enabling Service Hub community support
sections.summary: MSF launched the Enabling Service Hub in August last year to give persons with disabilities and caregivers closer community support and activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: Chairman, I appreciate the efforts of MSF in launching innovative new models like the Enabling Service Hub in August last year, which offer closer community support for persons with disabilities and their caregivers, closer to their home and bring partnership into the community to conduct more social activities and learning courses for persons with disabilities, befriending and caregiving support services, as well as outreach and reference to services that they need.

sections.label: CDC Vouchers donation to charities
sections.summary: CDC Vouchers can also be donated to charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: Today, Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers can also be donated to charities.

sections.label: Yearly review of EMP 2030
sections.summary: Speaker urges MSF to yearly review EMP 2030 to include developments like Healthier SG and cover inclusive insurance, criminal justice and mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: You see, the Singapore Government, for instance, has rolled out Healthier SG, Community Care Apartments, new Build-To-Order (BTO) towns, Active Ageing Centres, SkillsFuture upgrades, many, many exciting developments that I feel strongly can include the disability community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I therefore earnestly urge MSF to consciously conduct a formal yearly review, not just report, to update EMP 2030 so that it stays relevant and tap on these important, exciting developments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Certain critical areas not covered in EMP 2030 need attention, including inclusive insurance, criminal justice system for our special needs community, and the inclusion of mental health and neurodiversity conditions such as ADHD and dyslexia, all needed for a comprehensive support system for PwDs.

sections.label: Hybrid funding for disability services
sections.summary: Funding for day activity centres and residential homes should be re-evaluated, looking into a hybrid model of universal base and means-tested funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: The funding model for these services, for example, day activity centres and residential homes with moderate or severe disabilities, should be re-evaluated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: We should seriously look into a hybrid funding model comprising a universal base funding and means-tested funding quantum to address the core issue of insufficient funding for these essential services.

sections.label: Employment target for PwDs
sections.summary: The Enabling Master Plan 2030 tracks employment rate of PwDs, with an aspirational target of 40% of resident PwDs employed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: In the Enabling Master Plan 2030, efforts have also been put to track employment rate of PwDs, with an aspirational target employing of resident PwDs at 40%.

sections.label: PwD employment questions to MSF
sections.summary: Asks MSF what jobs PwDs are employed in, whether employer numbers are rising, which sectors, and if dominant sectors face market changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask MSF: one, what are the jobs that our PwDs are being employed in; two, whether the number of employers has been steadily increasing over the years and which sectors are these employers from; three, if there are some dominant sectors that our PwDs are employed in, are they facing market changes that will make the job roles of our PwDs more vulnerable?

sections.label: Sheltered workshop programme questions
sections.summary: Asks the number of PwDs entering the Sheltered Workshop to Work Programme annually in the last three years and how many return to sheltered workshops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, what is the number of PwDs entering the Sheltered Workshop to Work Programme annually in the last three years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, how many PwDs return to sheltered workshops after transitioning to open employment?

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant increase request
sections.summary: Asks whether MSF could consider increasing the monthly payout for caregiving parents under the Home Caregiving Grant given rising cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of our rising cost of living, could MSF consider increasing the monthly payout for caregiving parents under the Home Caregiving Grant?

sections.label: DPS applications decline
sections.summary: States that the number of DPS applications declined from 93 in 2015 to 20 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The number of DPS applications has declined from 93 in 2015 to 20 in 2023.

sections.label: Trusts and care plans developed
sections.summary: States that to date it has developed over 1,000 trusts and more than 3,000 care plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To date, it has developed over 1,000 trusts and developed more than 3,000 care plans.

sections.label: SG Enable vision and programmes
sections.summary: States SG Enable was formed as the focal agency for disability and inclusion and has developed infrastructure and programmes including job placement and caregiver support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chairman, SG Enable was formed with the noble vision of being the focal agency for disability and inclusion in Singapore and it has been critical in the implementation of the Enabling Masterplans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Over the years, various infrastructure and programmes for the special needs community had been developed under the auspices of SG Enable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This includes the job placement programme and the caregiver support programme as well as the Enabling Services Hub in Tampines and the Enabling Business Hub in Jurong.

sections.label: SG Enable support limitations
sections.summary: Asks whether the agency faces limitations in supporting families and whether support sufficiency and SG Enable's programme effectiveness have been assessed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Could I understand if there are limitations or challenges the agency faces in supporting the families especially if the resources are not available within the ecosystem?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Further, has there been an assessment of the sufficiency of support provided to the special needs community and the effectiveness of the services and programmes offered by SG Enable?

sections.label: SG Enable partnerships and resources
sections.summary: Asks whether SG Enable could leverage partnerships and better use community resources to close gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: As SG Enable continues in its efforts in the future, could it consider how best to leverage on partnerships and better utilise resources within the community to close the gaps?

sections.label: UOB inclusion outcomes
sections.summary: UOB's initiative since 2013 saw turnover fall from 50% to 5% and productivity rise 101% in its ScanHub department.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: UOB is one such company, reaping the inclusion reward since they started the initiative in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: They saw decreased turnover rate from 50% to 5%, and an improvement in productivity of 101% in their ScanHub department that utilises the methodical focus of persons with autism for repetitive tasks.

sections.label: Neurodiverse employers examples
sections.summary: GCHK promotes itself as a neurodiverse employer, and Gran Estación has persons with special needs making up about half its 120-strong workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: GCHK, UK's national security and intelligence agency, promotes itself as a neurodiverse employer to attract applicants such as persons with dyslexia, whom they find to have good visual awareness and better at spotting visual patterns that other people miss.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Gran Estación, a mall in Colombia, has persons with special needs making up roughly half of their 120-strong workforce.

sections.label: Autism numbers and stigma campaign
sections.summary: Over 5,500 per year since 2018 are found to have autism, and the speaker suggests a strengths-based public communications campaign.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: More than 5,500 since 2018 per year are found to have autism and this number is increasing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Let us bust the stigma of neurodiversity and the myths that employing them require more supervision, are costly to hire or that they are unsuitable for skilled jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I suggest that the Government invest in a "kick-ass" public communications campaign that takes a strengths-based and gift-based approach to the portrayal of these talents in our midst.

sections.label: Expansion and family resources
sections.summary: A programme in nine towns will expand to 18 by year end, with more parenting resources and a new marriage quiz tool.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Currently in nine towns, I am pleased to share that this will be expanded to 18 towns by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Ms Ng Ling Ling will be happy to note that the Council will roll out more parenting resources to better support families with teenagers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We have also launched a new self-help tool, Our Marriage Journey Quiz, last month, to help couples assess their relationship well-being akin to physical health checks.

sections.label: National Family Festival expansion
sections.summary: The FFL Council will expand the event to a month-long National Family Festival starting 25 May when school holidays begin.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: From this year, the FFL Council will expand the event to a month-long National Family Festival.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I encourage all families to make use of the FFL resources and participate in the National Family Festival, which will start from 25 May, when the school holidays begin.

sections.label: ComLink+ families family coach support
sections.summary: Of about 10,000 ComLink+ families working with us, 97% received family coach support as at end-2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Ms Denise Phua will be pleased to hear that of the approximately 10,000 ComLink+ families that have agreed to work with us, 97% are receiving family coach support as at end-2023.

sections.label: Family services review committee
sections.summary: MSF will establish a review committee on the Family Services Landscape, chaired by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua with sector partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Our vision is for families in need to receive support through a single primary touchpoint for family services, who can address the needs of different family members in a holistic and more coordinated manner to achieve better outcomes for the entire family.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that MSF will be establishing a review committee on the Family Services Landscape.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The committee will be chaired by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua and will comprise representatives from sector partners.

sections.label: Childcare subsidies for lower-income families
sections.summary: Lower-income families with monthly household income of $6,000 and below qualify for maximum childcare subsidies, benefiting up to 17,000 more children from Q4 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: All lower-income families with a monthly household income of $6,000 and below will qualify for the maximum amount of childcare subsidies for their income tier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Up to 17,000 additional children stand to benefit when we introduce this move from the fourth quarter of 2024.

sections.label: Preschool attendance by income
sections.summary: Children from lower-income families in Anchor Operator preschools have about 72% monthly attendance, lower than 79% for middle-income peers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: On average, among children who are enrolled in Anchor Operator preschools, children from lower-income families have a monthly attendance rate of about 72%, lower than the 79% attendance rate of their middle-income peers.

sections.label: KidSTART equipping parents
sections.summary: KidSTART, which has supported over 8,500 children, focuses on equipping parents with knowledge and skills to nurture their children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Even as we step up these efforts, we cannot overlook the importance of the home environment and parents' role in shaping their children's development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This is why KidSTART, which has supported more than 8,500 children to date, focuses on equipping parents with the knowledge and skills to nurture their children.

sections.label: Social service sector professionals needed
sections.summary: The social service sector needs 2,000 more professionals over the next five years to meet society's evolving needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To meet the evolving needs of our society, the social service sector needs 2,000 more professionals over the next five years.

sections.label: Social Service Sector Salary Guidelines review
sections.summary: Last year the Social Service Sector Salary Guidelines were reviewed for competitiveness, and around 80% of sector employees are paid within them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Last year, we reviewed the Social Service Sector Salary Guidelines to ensure salaries are competitive with comparable roles in competing markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Currently, around 80% of employees in the sector are paid within the salary guidelines.

sections.label: Year of Celebrating Volunteers
sections.summary: Building on partnerships with social service partners celebrated last year, 2024 is dedicated as the Year of Celebrating Volunteers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Last year, we celebrated the partnerships with our social service partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This year, we build on these partnerships and have dedicated 2024 as the Year of Celebrating Volunteers.

sections.label: Individual donations average $16 million
sections.summary: Collectively, these individual donations amass an average of $16 million per year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Collectively, these individual donations amass an average of $16 million per year.

sections.label: Matching donations to SHARE
sections.summary: The Government will continue matching new and incremental donations to SHARE for another two years till Financial Year 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To encourage more to give, the Government will continue to match new and incremental donations to SHARE.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will do so for another two years till Financial Year 2025.

sections.label: Matching customer and business donations
sections.summary: The Government matches 50 cents per customer dollar and another 50 cents if businesses match, extending this till Financial Year 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Government further multiplies the contributions by matching 50 cents to every dollar donated by customers, and another 50 cents to every dollar if businesses match their customer's donation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will extend this matching till Financial Year 2027.

sections.label: Low-income childcare fees
sections.summary: Lower-income families can pay as low as $3 per month for childcare in an Anchor Operator preschool.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Currently, lower-income families can pay as low as $3 per month for childcare in an Anchor Operator preschool.

sections.label: Childcare fee cap reductions
sections.summary: Childcare fee caps at Anchor and Partner Operators will be reduced by $40 in 2025, lowering fees for families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As announced by Deputy Prime Minister Wong in his Budget speech, we will further reduce childcare fee caps at Anchor and Partner Operators by $40 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: After subsidies, a middle-income working household with monthly income of $8,000, will pay $208 for full-day childcare at an Anchor Operator preschool from 2025, around 18% less from what they pay today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This will help us to achieve our 2019 National Day Rally commitment where families enrolled in Anchor Operators pay similar expenses to that of primary school and after-school student care, before means-tested subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are also on track to increasing the number of Government-supported preschool places so that 80% of preschoolers can have a place in a Government-supported preschool by around 2025, up from over 65% today.

sections.label: EC educator numbers
sections.summary: Since its launch in 2018, the number of EC educators has increased by more than 30% to 25,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2018, the number of EC educators has increased by more than 30% to 25,000.

sections.label: Enforcement levers and fines
sections.summary: ECDA will review enforcement levers and fines under the ECDC Act and enhance them through legislative changes if needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: ECDA will review enforcement levers and fines currently stipulated through the ECDC Act and will not hesitate to enhance the levers through legislative changes to take errant operators to task.

sections.label: Infant care places increase
sections.summary: About one in five infants are enrolled in infant care centres, with plans to add 9,000 places by 2030 and pilot childminding services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Currently, around one in five infants are enrolled in these infant care centres and we plan to increase centre-based infant care places by about 70%, or 9,000 more places by 2030 so that more parents can rely on this care option.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To complement these efforts, the Government will work with service providers to launch a three-year pilot in the second half of 2024 to provide affordable and reliable infant childminding services.

sections.label: Childminder infant limits
sections.summary: Under the pilot, each childminder may care for up to three infants at any one time, at their homes or a community space.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Under the pilot, each childminder will be allowed to care for up to three infants at any one time, at their homes or at a community space.

sections.label: Infant childminding service funding
sections.summary: ECDA will fund appointed operators to keep infant childminding out-of-pocket expenses affordable, aiming to match Anchor Operator infant care costs for middle-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To ensure that infant childminding services are affordable to families, ECDA will provide funding to appointed operators to keep the out-of-pocket expenses affordable for parents who use the service for their infants during typical working hours on weekdays.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We aim to make parents' expenses for childminding services similar to what a middle-income family pays for infant care at their Anchor Operator.

sections.label: EIPIC-Care caregiver training pilot
sections.summary: An EIPIC-Care pilot will be introduced to train caregivers of two- to three-year-olds with developmental needs to provide early intervention support at home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For parents to do this well, they will need to be equipped with the skills to provide early intervention support at home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This is why we will be introducing an EIPIC-Care pilot, a training programme for caregivers of two- to three-year-olds with developmental needs.

sections.label: Expanding early intervention centre capacity
sections.summary: 13 EIPIC-P and two EIPIC centres launched in 2023, four more centres in 2024, with Government-funded places to reach 80% by 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2023, we launched 13 EIPIC-P centres, which are operated by private providers; and two EIPIC centres, to increase our capacity by 1,200 places.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2024, we will launch four more early intervention centres and increase our capacity by 1,500 places.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will continue to expand our Government-funded places to serve 80% of children requiring medium to high levels of early intervention by 2027, up from 60% in 2022.

sections.label: SSCC expense decrease example
sections.summary: Families with monthly household income of $6,000 will see out-of-pocket SSCC expenses fall by one-third, from $500 to around $340.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To illustrate, families with a monthly household income of $6,000 will see one-third decrease in their out-of-pocket expenses paid for SSCC, from $500 to around $340.

sections.label: Infant safety background checks
sections.summary: ECDA will conduct background checks and require operators to meet service requirements to ensure the safety of infants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To ensure that the infants are well cared for, ECDA will conduct background checks and require operators to meet service requirements to ensure safety of the infants.

sections.label: Caregiver training and funded places
sections.summary: An EIPIC-Care pilot will train caregivers of two- to three-year-olds with developmental needs, and Government-funded places will increase for children with higher needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For parents to do this well, they will need to be equipped with the skills to provide early intervention support at home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This is why we will be introducing an EIPIC-Care pilot, a training programme for caregivers of two- to three-year-olds with developmental needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For children with higher needs, we will continue to increase the number of Government-funded places for children requiring medium- to high levels of early intervention support. : As Minister Masagos shared, all of us must play our part to realise our vision of a family-friendly society and a Singapore Made for Families.

sections.label: Celebrating Volunteers and Supporting Parents
sections.summary: 2024 is dedicated to celebrating volunteers, and the Government commits to supporting parents so every child can start well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As we dedicate 2024 as the Year of Celebrating Volunteers, let us appreciate and recognise the contributions, effort and sacrifice of our volunteers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are committed in supporting our parents and parents-to-be, so that they are assured that every child can have a good start in life in Singapore and that they have fair access to opportunities to progress in life.

sections.label: Social Service Offices Serve Families
sections.summary: Social Service Offices and Family Service Centres now serve 10,000 families with children in public rental flats across all 21 towns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Ms Denise Phua would be pleased to know that our Social Service Offices (SSOs) and Family Service Centres (FSCs) now serve 10,000 families with children in public rental flats in all 21 towns.

sections.label: Family Coaches and Volunteer Befrienders
sections.summary: MSF has about 120 family coaches, plans to recruit 200 more, and has trained about 1,600 volunteer befrienders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: MSF currently has about 120 family coaches and we plan to recruit 200 more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We have also recruited and trained about 1,600 volunteer befrienders working alongside our family coaches.

sections.label: ComLink+ Preschool Package
sections.summary: The ComLink+ Package for Preschool gives up to $3,700 in the CDA to children aged three to six who enrol in and attend preschool regularly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This is why the ComLink+ Package for Preschool will recognise parents' efforts to prioritise their children' preschool education.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This is how it will work: every child between ages three and six in a ComLink+ family who enrols in and attends preschool regularly, can receive up to $3,700 in their CDA.

sections.label: Government Matches CDA Top-ups
sections.summary: The Government will match CDA top-ups under the Baby Bonus Scheme, so a child can get as much as $7,400 in total.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The Government will also match these CDA top-ups as part of the Baby Bonus Scheme, so that the child can get as much as $7,400 in total in their CDA.

sections.label: Expanding ComLink+ to More Families
sections.summary: Over the next three years, ComLink+ will expand to cover another 3,000 lower-income families not in public rental housing who are eligible for KidSTART or UPLIFT.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From this month onwards, and over the next three years, we will expand ComLink+ to cover another 3,000 lower-income families who are not in public rental housing and are eligible for KidSTART or UPLIFT Community Network.

sections.label: DBS ComLink+ contribution
sections.summary: DBS contributed over $30 million to the ComLink+ Packages for Preschool and Home Ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: DBS, for instance, has made a contribution of over $30 million to the ComLink+ Packages for Preschool and Home Ownership.

sections.label: Place-and-Train disability employment
sections.summary: 131 employers hired over 330 persons with disabilities through Place-and-Train, which will be extended two years to train 200 more by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Through Place-and-Train, 131 employers have hired more than 330 persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will extend the programme for two more years and place and train another 200 persons with disabilities by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Last December, SG Enable launched the first Enabling Business Hub at Jurong, (EBH@Jurong), partnering employers, training providers and social service agencies, to bring job opportunities in the logistics sector closer to persons with disabilities in the West.

sections.label: Sheltered Workshop and employment rates
sections.summary: Sheltered Workshop capacity will rise by 500 spaces to 2,200 by 2030, and the employment rate of resident persons with disabilities rose from about 28% to 33%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As demand for Sheltered Workshop spaces remain high, we will increase capacity by 500 spaces, from the current 1,700 to 2,200 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will add 100 spaces to APSN's Centre for Adults this year, with the rest added progressively over the next few years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Because of the good uptake of the range of work opportunities, we raised the employment rate of resident persons with disabilities aged 15 to 64 from about 28% in 2018 to 2019, to 33% in 2022 to 2023, and we will press on towards our aspirational employment target of 40% by 2030.

sections.label: Day Activity Centre spaces
sections.summary: Day Activity Centres equip those unable to work with daily and community living skills, and 500 spaces will be added by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For those unable to work, our Day Activity Centres (DACs) help to equip them with essential daily and community living skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will add 500 DAC spaces, from the current 1,800 to 2,300 by 2030.

sections.label: Second and third ESH
sections.summary: The second and third ESH will launch in 2025, one in the North-East and one in the West.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Riding on this encouraging progress, we will launch the second and third ESH in 2025 – one in the North-East covering Punggol, Hougang, Sengkang and Serangoon; and one in the West focusing on Jurong West.

sections.label: ETS fees and subsidy threshold
sections.summary: About 40% of families receiving the ETS can expect out-of-pocket transport fee reductions of 10% or more, and the income threshold for means-tested subsidies will be updated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With this increase, about 40% of families currently receiving the ETS can expect a reduction in their out-of-pocket transport fees by 10% or more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Also, Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced that we will update the per capita household income threshold for means-tested subsidies so that more families can benefit from subsidies like the ETS.

sections.label: ComLink+ Progress Package support
sections.summary: The ComLink+ Progress Package recognises and supplements ComLink+ families' efforts towards employment, financial stability, home ownership and children's education, with a first preschool package launching this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: ComLink+ Progress Package recognises and supplements ComLink+ families' efforts in working towards stable employment, financial stability, home ownership and giving their children a good start in education.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will launch the first ComLink+ package for preschool this year to encourage early enrolment and regular attendance.

sections.label: Support for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: Employment support programmes for PwDs are extended, with more Sheltered Workshop capacity, more Day Activity Centres spaces and two new Enabling Services Hubs in the North-East and West.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We also continue to support PwDs, by providing different employment support programmes catering to varying needs and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This includes extending the Place-and-Train Programme and increasing capacity for Sheltered Workshops.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Aside from employment, we support PwDs to live independently and better integrate into the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will increase the number of Day Activity Centres spaces and launch two new Enabling Services Hub in the North-East and West later this year, providing more opportunities for PwDs to engage in social activities and learn new skills.

sections.label: Review of social service master plans
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a structured official review each year to ensure eight-year master plans in the social service sector are updated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: So, I really think that eight-year master plans in the social service sector definitely have to be updated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: So, can I ask for a structured official review each year so that we can ensure that these plans are updated?

sections.label: Commitment to ComLink+ families
sections.summary: The speaker commits that MSF and its officers, down to the SSOs on the ground, will help every ComLink+ family currently served.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: So, while I cannot — well, I can, but I would definitely use up all the clarification time going through all the details of the various implementation bumps that we have encountered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: But you have my commitment in this Chamber that MSF and our officers, right down the line to the SSOs on the ground, will commit to helping every single ComLink+ families that we are serving today.

sections.label: Employment outcome indicators
sections.summary: Employment indicators target 40% employment, up from about 30% to 31% when EMP 2030 launched in 2022, translating to about 10,000 job placements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Some of the indicators that we look at pertains specifically to outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: So, for instance, in terms of employment, getting to 40% employment, and that translates, from when we first started in 2022, when the EMP 2030 was launched, we were at about 30%, 31%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: And to make that leap from 30% to 40%, that translates to about 10,000 job placements.

sections.label: Disability and Inclusion Panel Study
sections.summary: NCSS conducts a quality of life survey of persons with disabilities called the Disability and Inclusion Panel Study.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Other outcomes that we look at, NCSS conducts a quality of life survey of persons with disabilities and this is called the Disability and Inclusion Panel Study.

sections.label: Lower-income families in Family Month
sections.summary: MSF is asked how it plans to encourage lower-income families, especially those with children in rental flats, to join Family Month activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: How does MSF plan to encourage, to facilitate lower-income families, in particular, families with children living in rental flats, to participate in the family month activities?

sections.label: Kinderland supervision and staffing
sections.summary: MSF found inadequate supervision by centre leaders and oversight by employees, shortened Kinderland centres' tenure, and monitors on-site, citing strict teacher-student ratios.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: What we have found was that there was inadequate supervision by centre leaders and that there was oversight by the employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And we have shortened the tenure for the Kinderland centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We are also actively monitoring, going down on-site to supervise what is happening in the preschool.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, I do not see it as a general insufficient resourcing in the sector as a whole because MSF has very strict requirements on teacher and student ratios.

sections.label: Reviewing legislation and financial penalties
sections.summary: Legislation is being reviewed and levers enhanced, possibly through enhanced financial penalties, to signal that abuse is not taken lightly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We are reviewing those legislation and we will enhance those levers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: It could take the form of enhanced financial penalties so that there is a very clear signal to the industry that we do not take such abuse lightly.

sections.label: Childminding fees and out-of-pocket expenses
sections.summary: The aim is for parents' childminding expenses to be similar to a medium-income family's infant care at Anchor Operators, with potential out-of-pocket expenses about $700.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Where fees are concerned, I shared that we aim to make parents' expenses for childminding services similar to what a medium-income family pays for infant care at Anchor Operators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, the potential out-of-pocket expenses could be about $700 thereabouts.

sections.label: Employment of persons with disabilities
sections.summary: With the Enabling Business Hub in Jurong launched last year, job support services for PwDs increased from one year to two years and intensity increased where needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
sentences.text: I ask this because I do share your concern and perhaps those of other Members as well, that we might become too fixated on the EMP 2030 target of 40% employment and inadvertently neglect stability of open employment of PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I think a quick point to note is that with the launch of the Enabling Business Hub in Jurong last year, we have facilitated an increase of job support services that is provided to PwDs from one year to two years and the intensity of job support services is actually increased, where needed.

sections.label: EIPIC capacity and early intervention
sections.summary: A six-month home programme is described, and EIPIC capacity rose by 1,200 places in 2023 and will rise by 1,500 places with four more centres in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Could she elaborate more on what this is?

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: And secondly, the point on capacity building, because I understand that right now the waiting time for children with high needs to be enrolled into an EIPIC centre can be several months and it is a bit ironic because we are looking at early intervention in a very critical few years in their lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: So, will the Ministry be looking into shoring up in immediate-term manpower in this sector by, perhaps, attracting talents and well-trained professionals from abroad to shore up our local capacity and then to look into capability building in the next three to five years to quickly tap on local talents to make sure that the EIPIC provisions and services can be ramped up in an accelerated manner?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And this happens, this can happen at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This will be a six-month programme and the caregivers will be learning from professionals through group workshops and individual coaching sessions on how to support their child's development at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On her second question, I had shared that we are launching more places when it comes to EIPIC, by increasing our capacity by 1,200 places.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This was in 2023 and this was already a 26% increase from 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And in 2024, we will launch four more early intervention centres and increase our capacity by 1,500 places.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And if you look at it in terms of percentage, we are expanding our Government-funded places to serve the children from 60% of children who require medium to high levels of early intervention moving from 60% coverage to 80% coverage.

sections.label: Childminder engagement and FSC funding
sections.summary: Operators, not MSF, will engage and be responsible for childminders, and FSC funding and family coach visits were discussed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Based on the engagements so far, the intent is for the operators to engage the childminders and be responsible for the childminders, because it would be very difficult for MSF to be regulating each and every childminder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, the short answer to your question is, yes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: But I would like to ask if the Ministry would consider reviewing the current funding model of FSCs to transition towards an outcomes-based funding for those FSCs that work on social mobility outcomes, rather than the current model which is based on the caseload funding?

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: As I had mentioned in my speech, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua is now leading a task force to conduct an overall review of the FSC landscape and certainly, the area our Member mentioned just now will be one of the areas that he will be looking at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In my excitement, I said that the family coaches would visit the families at the beginning, once or twice every month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Actually, it is once, every one to two months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: What manifests on the surface is often the result of layers upon layers of varied issues.
